sources.title: Local Japanese pre-English catalog: Nivi City Gym / Brock
PokéCardex: Nivi City Gym set page

Local pre-English symbol-status matrix
Japanese pre-English release map

claims.text: The local catalog and Japanese pre-English release map model Nivi City Gym / Brock as released on April 26, 1998.
The local catalog models the product as a 60-card deck plus 4 additional cards, while its unique-row catalog exposure is 25 rows.
Bulbapedia describes Nivi City Gym as a Japanese-exclusive Standard Deck that complements Leaders' Stadium and provided the basis for the English Brock Theme Deck.
Bulbapedia notes that Brock's Onix, Brock's Rhyhorn, Brock's Sandslash, and Brock's Zubat became notorious common rares in Gym Heroes because of their fixed rarity in this deck.
The local symbol-status matrix records Nivi City Gym / Brock as a real missing-symbol lane, but not a Base No Rarity source.

The local attention rows include Brock's Zubat, Brock's Vulpix, Brock's Sandshrew, Brock's Sandslash, Brock's Geodude, Brock's Onix, Brock, Brock's Training Method, Pewter City Gym, and Double Colorless Energy.
The local artist clusters are led by Ken Sugimori and Keiji Kinebuchi, with smaller Atsuko Nishida, Benimaru Itoh, and Sumiyoshi Kizuki contributions.

Nivi City Gym / Brock matters because it turns a Gym Leader into a complete play apparatus: the Pokémon are not merely species, they are Brock's team, Brock's training, Brock's city, and Brock's deck constraints made physical.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, or agent memory says Nivi City Gym, Brock deck, ニビシティジム タケシ, Brock's Onix, Brock's Zubat, common rare, missing rarity, or No Rarity.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Preserve the gym-deck product boundary: 64-card product context, 25 unique catalog rows, missing-symbol deck lane, not Base No Rarity.
steps: Preserve release_family_id jp_tcg_nivi_city_gym_brock_19980426 and the Japanese gym-deck context.
Do not treat the 25 unique catalog rows as proof that the sealed product contains only 25 cards; the local product note and Bulbapedia deck list point to a 64-card product context.
Do not collapse missing-symbol deck cards into 1996 Base No Rarity; this is a Gym deck missing-symbol lane.
Preserve owner-name identity: Brock's Onix, Brock's Geodude, Brock's Training Method, and Pewter City Gym are not ordinary species or generic trainer rows.
For common-rare or Gym Heroes carryover claims, require the exact Japanese deck row and the later English row to be named separately.

narrative.why_it_matters: Nivi City Gym is where the binder stops treating Brock as a character and starts treating him as infrastructure. The creatures belong to him, the city belongs to him, even the training method belongs to him. It is wonderfully specific: a 1998 Japanese deck object that turns Gym Leader identity into play, then later leaves strange fossils of itself in English Gym Heroes common rares. The charm is not chase gloss. It is ownership becoming grammar.
